{{Short description|Example of the Koszul duality}}

In mathematics, the '''Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand correspondence''' or '''BGG correspondence''' for short is the first example of the [[Koszul duality]].<ref>J.-W. He and Q.-S. Wu. “Koszul differential graded algebras and BGG correspondence”. In: J. Algebra 320.7 (2008), pp. 2934–2962. arXiv: 0712.1324. url: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2008.06.021.</ref>

Established by [[Joseph Bernstein]], [[Israel Gelfand]], and Sergei Gelfand,<ref>[[Joseph Bernstein]], [[Israel Gelfand]], and Sergei Gelfand. ''Algebraic bundles over <math>P^n</math> and problems of linear algebra''. Funkts. Anal. Prilozh. 12 (1978); English translation in Functional Analysis and its Applications 12 (1978), 212-214</ref> the correspondence is an explicit triangulated equivalence that relates the bounded [[derived category]] of [[coherent sheaves]] on the projective space <math>\mathbb{P}(V)</math> and the [[stable category]] of graded modules <math>\operatorname{gr} \wedge V</math> over the [[exterior algebra]] <math>\wedge V</math>; i.e.,
:<math>D^b(\mathbb{P}(V)) \simeq \overline{\operatorname{gr} \wedge V}</math>.

In the noncommutative setting, Martínez Villa and Saorín generalized the BGG correspondence to finite-dimensional [[self-injective]] [[Koszul algebras]] <math>A </math> with [[coherent sheaf|coherent]] Koszul duals <math>A^{!}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Martínez Villa |first1= Roberto |last2= Saorín |first2= Manuel |date= 2004 |title= Koszul Equivalence and Dualities |url= https://msp.org/pjm/2004/214-2/pjm-v214-n2-p09-p.pdf |journal= Pacific Journal of Mathematics |volume= 214 |issue= 2|publisher= |pages= 359–378 |doi= |access-date= 14 May 2025}}</ref> Roughly speaking, they proved that the stable category of finite-dimensional graded modules over a finite-dimensional self-injective Koszul algebra <math>A</math> is triangulated equivalent to the bounded derived category of the tails category of the Koszul dual <math>A^{!}</math> (when <math>A^{!}</math> is coherent).
